fields.title: The strategy-review packet grades edge off live in-window n, which the binding promotion-evidence rule forbids
fields.note: OPERATOR-DIRECTED 2026-09-09. ⚠️ THIS NOTE WAS REWRITTEN THE SAME DAY BECAUSE ITS FIRST VERSION WAS THE WRONG SHAPE. It read "DO NOT RE-ASK THE WINDOW/FLOOR QUESTION IN ANY FORM", and the operator rejected that framing outright: "you keep adding guards in the shape of forbidding questions from being asked - this is incorrect. the problem isn't the question, it's the underlying misunderstanding of infra and processes, and not asking questions isn't what fixes that - it just makes it more likely that you will f****** again in the future because you're not asking the right question... it's that you don't understand how the system works. that's what we need to fix here, not the question". THE PROHIBITION IS RETRACTED. Ask whatever you need to, window and floor included. Banning a question suppresses the symptom and leaves the misunderstanding intact, so the next session fails in a NEW way instead of asking a better question. THE THING TO CARRY IS THE MODEL, NOT A RULE: (1) EDGE is established OFFLINE — this repo has extensive backtesting infrastructure built for exactly that (purged walk-forward CV, replay_pregate_fleet, the point-in-time backfills), and that is where 'does this strategy work' is answered. (2) LIVE data establishes MECHANICS ONLY — that executions match the simulator — which canon says needs 1-2 executed trades, not calendar time. (3) SLOW LIVE ACCRUAL IS A FEATURE OF THE SYSTEM, NOT A BARRIER TO OVERCOME: a leg closing ~1.2 trades a week is not a problem to engineer around, and `none_gradeable` on a live window is not a defect. (4) Fewer legs does NOT raise trades-per-leg, and on paper accounts every leg runs regardless — the manager recommended that lever and the operator rejected it. WHAT THE WORK ACTUALLY IS: the review/validation layer is built on a LIVE-ACCRUAL model of evidence while the system's real evidence engine is the BACKTEST infrastructure. MIN_CLOSED_FOR_ACTION is a symptom of that mismatch, not the defect. The operator's own framing: "our overall operation is clearly not built to suit the system's structure." THE RULE THIS CONTRADICTS ALREADY EXISTS AND IS BINDING: docs/CLAUDE-RULES-CANONICAL.md § 'Promotion evidence — offline edge, live mechanics' (2026-07-26), scope explicitly STRATEGY legs, clause 3 'No gate may require calendar-time accrual to prove edge', and it already names this as 'the recurring drift this rule kills'. THE GUARD HALF MUST ENFORCE THE RULE, NOT A PHRASE: a gate producing a STRATEGY verdict must source its edge from offline evidence. A guard that greps for forbidden words is the same wrong shape one level down. Keep the positive control — a guard silent because it scans nothing is indistinguishable from one silent because all is well. Tier-3 where it changes what a KILL/DEMOTE rests on: propose, do not enact. Retiring a strategy leg is Tier-3 and is not the answer here. Manager does not take this — it is ROUTED to session_01MrTjuoRpBb7spyQLydXmmT, which has been sent this correction directly.

fields.title: Decision PRESENTATION on ClaudeBot: options as a readable list, and real multiple choice
fields.tier: 2 (touches the Telegram bridge; no order path, no strategy config, no risk caps)
fields.raised_by: operator, 2026-09-02, in conversation, EXPLICITLY not urgent: 'Also not urgent, but something that I do want us to have ... somewhere in our work plan.'
fields.observed: Operator, on the live decision prompt: 'the point with the buttons is that it's very shortened, a little cut off ... maybe there's more of a list and I can click the options, maybe some would be multiple choice. I think that button is a good first step, but probably not the end of where this design needs to go.' So the ASK half of the decision round-trip works and its PRESENTATION is the limit.
fields.⚠️_the_truncation_is_the_LABEL_not_the_c: DO NOT go looking for a callback_data size bug -- it is already solved and re-solving it would waste the session. `callback_data` is 26 bytes FIXED (`wdec:<12 hex>:<8 hex>`) against Telegram's 64-byte cap, and it carries a DIGEST of the option KEY, deliberately never a positional index. What the operator sees cut off is the BUTTON LABEL, which Telegram renders narrow and elides. Those are different layers.

the_shape_to_build.1_options_as_a_numbered_list_in_the_MESS: Put the full option text in the message body as a numbered list -- where there is room for it -- and reduce each button to its number. The body is not width-constrained the way a button is, so the option a person is choosing between becomes readable without touching the callback contract at all. This is the cheap half and it is probably most of the win.
the_shape_to_build.2_multiple_choice_is_NOT_one_press: [!] A single inline keyboard press submits ONE value, so multi-select is not a formatting change -- it needs a TOGGLE keyboard: each tap flips an option's mark and re-renders the keyboard, and an explicit Submit sends the set. That means holding PARTIAL, UNSUBMITTED state between taps, which the current design deliberately does not have. Decide where that state lives BEFORE building it; a half-submitted answer that looks submitted is the forward-failure the transit contract exists to refuse.
the_shape_to_build.3_free_text_is_still_a_separate_step: Unchanged and deliberately not half-built: inline buttons cannot carry arbitrary text. A request declaring no options is still SENT (so a blocking question is never invisible) and says plainly that it needs an answer on the SPA or in the repo.

fields.what_must_not_regress: The four never-collapsed answer states (`not_submitted`/`in_transit`/`committed`/`unreadable`); the option token staying a KEY DIGEST rather than an index (an index silently records a different answer if the object is reordered between send and tap); the fail-closed write gate; and the confirmation continuing to read 'Submitted -- NOT yet decided'.
fields.why_deferred: P1 is the handoff capability and P2 is the overhaul implementation. This is a UX improvement to a channel that already works end-to-end -- the round-trip was observed complete on 2026-09-02. The operator said not urgent and this records that as a decision, not as an oversight.

fields.title: 21 stale queue rows will re-fire WITH bodies once #10747 lands and the VM is re-provisioned
fields.detail: docs/claude/pending-pings.jsonl holds 21 rows that render today as bare event labels. #10747 makes the renderer emit real bodies. The dedupe ledger that suppresses re-sends (runtime_logs/pending_pings_delivered) is VM-LOCAL and gitignored, so a re-provision would replay all 21 -- this time with content -- as one burst on the channel we just made trustworthy.
fields.operator_decision: 2026-09-02: MARK THEM DELIVERED, KEEP THE ROWS. The operator chose the record-preserving option over pruning, on the grounds that these 21 rows ARE the evidence base for the 42%-bare-label finding and pruning them would destroy the proof of the bug just as it is fixed. The stamp must say WHICH state it is asserting: they were delivered EMPTY, and stamping a bare 'delivered' would be a false claim.
fields.note: Dispatch AFTER #10747 merges -- it touches scripts/notify_on_pull.py and would conflict.
fields.⚠️_I_MARKED_THIS_OWNED_BEFORE_IT_WAS: CORRECTED 2026-09-02T09:20Z. I set state=in_flight and owner='subagent:stale-ping-delivered-stamp' in the same edit that unblocked it, and then DID NOT SPAWN. For ~5 minutes the checklist asserted an owner that did not exist. ⚠️ That is the same class as MI-15 (the registry claiming sessions it did not have) and it is worse in this direction: a row reading in_flight WITH AN OWNER is one a successor skips, so a false owner does not just lose information, it actively diverts attention away from real work. State is `ready` — unblocked, decided, nobody on it.
fields.why_not_spawned_yet: Two sub-sessions cannot share one git working tree: they would fight over checkouts and `git add -A` from either can sweep the other's uncommitted files into the wrong branch — a hazard that already nearly bit this session, whose `git status` surfaced the AVAX agent's in-progress test file on an unrelated workflow branch. Agent worktree isolation was ATTEMPTED and REFUSED here: 'Cannot create agent worktree: not in a git repository' — the session's cwd is /home/user while the repo is /home/user/Metis-Insights. So this waits for the AVAX sub-session to finish, or goes to a cloud session with its own container (create_session), which must be REGISTERED IN SESSIONS.json in the same action.
fields.risk_is_real_but_not_imminent: Firing requires the VM-local gitignored ledger to be LOST (re-provision / re-clone / fresh data dir). It is not on a timer. So deferring is defensible; leaving a false owner on it was not.
fields.deferred_reason: Not tied to P1 (handoff) or P2 (overhaul implementation). Keeps its state and evidence; not worked until the priorities are done. A P0 incident overrides this immediately.
